items.name: Prepare the image
items.description: Crops, straightens, rotates or brightens a page and keeps the result as a new version of the image; the original is never changed. Damaged or faded pages read far better prepared. Every later step reads the prepared version, and you can always go back to the scan as it came.
items.compare: the renditions side by side

items.name: Split pages
items.description: Cuts a scan of an open book (two pages at once) into single pages, in order. Each half becomes a page of its own, so lines are found and read on one page at a time and the reading order runs from the left page to the right.
items.compare: the cut pages side by side

items.name: Find regions
items.description: Finds the blocks on a page (main text, margins, tables, headings, drawings) so each kind can be read the right way. A layout detector such as YOLO helps when pages mix kinds; on plain running text, finding the lines alone is usually enough.
items.compare: the shapes side by side, with precision and recall against shapes a person has checked

items.name: Find lines
items.description: Finds each line of writing and its baseline, so a line reader can read it. Kraken does this on your Mac for free.
items.compare: the shapes side by side, with precision and recall against shapes a person has checked

items.name: Put in order
items.description: Works out the order the lines are read in, across columns and margins. The order is kept as a named reading order, so a second order (the margins first, say) can sit beside it.
items.compare: the two orders side by side

items.name: Refine shapes
items.description: Tightens rough boxes from one model with a more precise detector. Vision models often place lines roughly; a detector run afterwards keeps the same lines and fits their shapes to the writing.
items.compare: the shapes side by side, with precision and recall against shapes a person has checked

items.name: Find signs
items.description: Finds each sign on a tablet, seal or page, for scripts read sign by sign. Used for cuneiform, hieroglyphs, Linear B and scripts not yet deciphered, where a line is not the unit that is read.
items.compare: the shapes side by side, with precision and recall against shapes a person has checked

items.name: Find a table's cells
items.description: Finds the rows, columns and cells of a table. Each cell becomes a segment of its own, with its row, column and any span, so it can be read and exported as a spreadsheet.
items.compare: the shapes side by side, with precision and recall against shapes a person has checked

items.name: Read each line
items.description: Reads each line on its own. Line readers (Kraken, Tesseract for print) are fast, run on your Mac, and can be trained on your own corrected pages.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Read the whole page
items.description: Reads a whole page at once, usually with a vision model. Strong on hard pages, but it does not keep where each line was.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Tie text to lines
items.description: Places a page's text onto its found lines, line by line, so each line knows its words. This is what lets a page read by a vision model be corrected and trained on line by line.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Review the reading
items.description: A second model checks each reading against the picture and proposes corrections, kept as new readings beside the first. It can be limited to the lines the first reader was unsure of, which saves time and money on long runs.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Trace a drawing
items.description: Redraws a drawing, map or seal as a clean vector picture. The tracing is kept as a reading of the drawing's segment, beside the picture it came from.
items.compare: the drawings side by side

items.name: Identify signs
items.description: Proposes which sign each mark is, with how sure it is, for a person to confirm. The proposals are checked against the project's sign list; nothing is settled until you confirm it.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Transcribe speech
items.description: Turns recorded speech into text with its timings. Each stretch of text keeps the moment it was spoken, so the recording can be played from any line.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Translate, transliterate or normalise
items.description: Makes a second reading in modern spelling, another script or another language, beside the original, never over it. What was written stays the record; the second reading is for searching, reading aloud or publishing.
items.compare: a text diff of the readings, with character and word error rates where pages are corrected

items.name: Find documents in a folder
items.description: Proposes which pages belong together as one document, such as a letter of three pages in an archive bundle, for you to confirm. It reads the text already there: a court's caption, a heading, a place and date, a greeting open a document; a signature or "Cópiese, notifíquese" closes one; a sentence running over the page joins two pages. Blank backs and pages photographed twice are reported, not made documents. Each proposed document has its kind (Sentencia, Carta, Cable …) and how sure it is. An accepted document becomes one document with its pages in order; by default only the clearest are accepted by themselves and the rest wait for you, and one undo puts them back.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Split into entries
items.description: Splits a diary, register or ledger into its dated entries. Each entry becomes a segment with its date, so it can be found, sorted and placed on a timeline.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Find names
items.description: Finds the people, places, dates and things named in the text. How well a tagger does depends on the language; each name found is tied to the words it came from, for you to confirm or correct.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Find statements
items.description: Finds who did what to whom (sold, gave, owed, married), each tied to the words it came from. These statements are what the knowledge graph is built from, and each one can be checked.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Work out dates
items.description: Turns dates as written (feast days, regnal years, any calendar) into exact dates. How it works: rules, not a model. Fichero reads the date at the head of each page (or the date its catalogue gives), and converts it through tested calendar libraries (Julian, Hebrew, Islamic, French Republican) and tables of regnal years and eras. A date known only to the month or the year is kept as a span, so it still sorts in the right place. The date as written stays beside the worked-out one, with how certain it is; a page that says it is undated ("s.f.") is marked so, never given a guess. Runs on this Mac, free.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Link to authorities
items.description: Proposes links from people and places to Wikidata, VIAF, GeoNames or your own list, for you to confirm. A confirmed link lets your people and places be matched with other projects and published as linked data.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Place in a gazetteer
items.description: Gives each place its coordinates and a gazetteer identifier, naming the gazetteer. Placed names can be shown on a map and searched by where they are.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Make vectors for search
items.description: Lets you search by meaning, not only by words. Chosen for your languages.
items.compare: each model's top results for a few of your own questions

items.name: Describe for the catalogue
items.description: Proposes values for your catalogue fields from the page, for you to confirm. Facts only.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Extract to a table
items.description: Fills one row per document or entry with your fields (for a sale record: seller, buyer, the person sold, price, date, place), each value tied to its text; exports as a spreadsheet. The fields, and the question each one asks, come from the kind of document you choose, so every row has the same columns. A value a person typed is never replaced; "not on this page" is kept as an answer, never a guess.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Pull out passages
items.description: Gathers the passages on a question or theme, each with its source. The passages are collected into a note you can keep writing in.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Train a model
items.description: Trains a small model on your corrected pages, so it reads your material better and faster. A Kraken reader or a YOLO detector trains on this Mac; larger models on Hugging Face Jobs or a cluster, if the project lets pages leave the Mac.
items.compare: the candidate against the current step on held-out corrected pages

items.name: Check
items.description: A person or a checker model confirms, corrects or rejects each proposal of a layer, with its reasons; a model's check is recorded as that model's, never as a person's. Which layer it checks (readings, names, statements, links) is a setting of the step.
items.compare: the two lists side by side, with precision and recall where a person has confirmed some

items.name: Export
items.description: Writes your work out in the formats you name (TEI, PAGE, ALTO, plain text, Markdown, Excel, RDF, a website), kept up to date if you choose a synced folder. Every format is written from the same record, with where each piece came from.
items.compare: the files side by side

items.name: Publish
items.description: Publishes a folder as IIIF or a static website. Others can then read the pages, and link to them, without Fichero.
items.compare: the published pages side by side
